title.narrative: BAHIA ROAD REHABILITATION AND MAINTENANCE PROJECT - 2ND PHASE

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to enhance, in a sustainable fashion, road accessibility and safety in selected regions of the State of Bahia territory.

The development objective of the Second Phase of the Bahia Road Rehabilitation and Maintenance Project for Brazil is to enhance, in a sustainable fashion, road accessibility and safety in selected regions of the state of Bahia's territory. The project comprises of five components. The first component, institutional strengthening supports the sustainability strand of the project development objective (PDO). It includes five sub-components: (i) new options for road financing; (ii) road asset management; (iii) road administration efficiency; (iv) logistics planning; and (v) transport investment impact assessment. The second component, performance-based state highway rehabilitation and maintenance supports the sustainability and road safety dimensions of the PDO. It includes two sub-components: (i) rehabilitation and maintenance work through performance-based contracts for rehabilitation and road maintenance (CREMA) on about 1,685 kilometers (km) of identified sections of Bahia's paved highways, including road rehabilitation and maintenance; and (ii) rehabilitation and maintenance works through CREMA- public-private partnership (PPP) or CREMA contracts on about 685 km of identified sections of the Borrower's paved highways, including, road rehabilitation and maintenance. The third component, feeder road improvement supports the accessibility dimension of the PDO. It will provide support to improve road accessibility in Bahia through the carrying out of works to eliminate about 900 critical spots on selected municipal rural roads in 62 selected municipalities (the municipal road subprojects), including, among other things: (i) improving the drainage of the platform, including the replacement of existing unsafe wood bridges with concrete standardized bridges; (ii) constructing and or reconstructing culverts and longitudinal drainage; and (iii) constructing fords and eliminating quagmires. The fourth component, road safety supports the road safety dimension of the PDO, through institutional strengthening and road safety corridors. It includes two sub-components: (i) institutional strengthening; and (ii) road safety corridors. The fifth component, project management will finance the project coordination unit consulting and operating costs for project monitoring, supervision, and evaluation, including audits.

title.narrative: Elimination of physical critical spots for road safety on the selected corridors

comment.narrative: <p>At the time of closing, the works were ongoing to eliminate critical spots for road safety on the two selected corridors (87km).The pilot corridors had delays in the procurement process, resulting in works only starting in March 2022, and as a result, no critical points were actually eliminated on those two roads by the closing date. Works are advancing and will finish in May 2023. However, critical points were eliminated from other roads (creation of roundabouts, improvement of intersections) and in rural roads,so in other regions, improvements could be measured. In addition, enforcement was improved along several critical roads, including this, with major results, like on the Rodovia Verde - BA-099. </p>

<p>The number of km that was fully rehabilitated by the closing date was 2979 km, exceeding the original target of 2370 km (as shown in Table A9.6 – annex 9). In total, the State of Bahia has ongoing contracts for rehabilitation and maintenance of 3954 km, almost 4000 km. </p>

title.narrative: Number of yearly meetings conducted by the Infrastructure Committee on the Bahia Industries' Federation.

comment.narrative: <p>The target was exceeded. The State logistics discussions happened within the "Federacao das Industrias da Bahia" (Bahia Industries' Federation), a private sector forum that served the same purpose that the State Logistics Committee (theoriginal forum of discussions replaced with Bahia Industries’ Federation in R21) was expected to serve at the time of designing the Project. The state government had a permanent representative of the Secretariat of Infrastructure in this private forum. Three meetings were made during the last year. Only during 2020 meetings did not happen. </p>

title.narrative: People with enhanced access to transportation services

comment.narrative:
<p>The project achievements remained slightly under the target.</p>

<p>The R21 added a new Corporate Indicator to measure the number of direct and indirect beneficiaries of the rehabilitated CREMA roads (the original target of 2,370km under Component 2), the feeder road interventions (the original target of 900 spot improvement interventions under Component 3), and the road safety corridors (road safety works along 87km on two corridors under Component 4) amounting to 6,183,000 beneficiaries.</p>

<p>The final number reached a large population thanks to the additional roads rehabilitated that included the following 2979 km rehabilitated as of projectclosing: It is expected that the remaining population will get enhanced access to transportation when (a) the balance of 1,025 km has been rehabilitated under the State funding by May 2023, (b) the 299 additional critical spots have been improved under the State of Bahia in all four consortia by March 2023; and (c) the road safety corridors will be completed with counterpart funds by May 2023.</p>

title.narrative: Cumulated number of municipalities where citizens engaged in road investment definition and prioritization

comment.narrative: <p>The project exceeded the target and engaged with 64 municipalities to get input on defining and prioritizing road investments to implement the works for improving rural road accessibility. </p>

title.narrative: Hours of Capacity Building for improving the business model for SEINFRA/SIT

comment.narrative:
<p>This project highly exceeded the target for the revised indicator (see Annex 7).</p>

<p>When the COVID-19 pandemic hit, only 2000 hours had been carried out, but during 2021 and 2022 the project achieved and exceeded the target for training covering road safety training, Environmental & Social training, etc. In total, more than 400 staff were trained in the program. </p>

<p>Additionally, 167 courses or workshops were provided in relation to environmental and social topics, reaching more than 30,000 people during the project implementation and across the different state regions – not counted in this indicator. </p>

title.narrative: Cumulated number of critical spots eliminated

comment.narrative: <p>The total number of rural road spot improvements completed exceeded the original target. The project contracted 1285 spot improvements during the project life under the project. The project is expected to complete the remaining spot improvements (299) outof the total 1285 spot improvements that were contracted during the project on State's funding during the upcoming months (until March 2023). Public Consultations were finished by 2019. </p>

title.narrative: State paved road network under performance-based rehabilitation and maintenance contracts

comment.narrative:
<p>The project exceeded the target for the state paved road network under performance-based rehabilitation and maintenance contracts. When the project started, only 3 percent of the state paved road was under Rehabilitation and Maintenance contracts. The project interventions contributed to this result: 3954 km contracted: 3,407 km under five-year CREMA contracts and 547 of BA 052 CREMA-PPP. An additional 374 km of concessions are outside of the Project Scope, making it a total of 4,328 km with Performance-based contracts in Bahia. Table A9.6 shows the information in annex 9. </p>

<p>*It is important to note that the baseline was measured against a 10,900 km value of the previous paved road State network, meaning that the State was able to implement 1300 km of newly paved roads during the project. The actual value would be 38 percent of the baseline 10,900 km value.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Share of rural population with access to an all-season road

comment.narrative:
<p>The project increased the share of the rural population with access to an all-season road above the target.</p>

<p>The number of inhabitants in the 4 selected regions with year-round rural road accessibility improvements to be implemented was at baseline 490.000 - meaning only 45 % of the population in those 4 areas had all-season accessibility. </p>

<p>In year 4 (2020), it reached 50% - 655.556 inhabitants, and in year 6 (2022) it reached 65% - 852.223, larger than the original target – 787,000,but short of the revised target of 1,315,000 (as this number was targeting all the population of the 64 municipalities). The project contributed to this result by completing 986 critical spot improvements by the project closing.</p>

<p>The State is completing the improvement of 299 additional critical spots by March 2023 (1190 interventions completed by November 2022); this increases the spot improvements to 1,285 and the number of rural people with access to an all-season road to 70 percent.  </p>

<p>The total population of the 64 municipalities that benefited from the improvement of the rural roads was 1,315,000 inhabitants (or 7,5 % of the State population) out of which 852,000 inhabitants have all-season access. </p>

<p> </p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Roads in good and fair condition as a share of total classified roads

comment.narrative: <p>The project exceeded the target. This indicator measures the percentage of the total classified road network in the project area that is in good and fair condition depending on the road surface and the level of roughness. The percentage of roads in good and far condition (IRI < 5) of the total paved network in the project areas improved from 80% to 88 %, one of the best in Brazil. It is a significant result, considering that the total network increased from 10,900 km to 12,800 km. </p>

title.narrative: Establishment of the State Infrastructure Road Fund

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved in 2019 (the third year of implementation). The fund is supporting the increase in the paved network of the State and other road interventions. Now, with the new project in preparation, there is a need to use this to implement the Pro-active Maintenance aspects during the next decades.</p>

title.narrative: Establishment of a State Committee for road safety

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved. The Committee was established in September 2016. CETRAN will be the main agency for Road Safety in the State. </p>

title.narrative: Operationalization of integrated traffic accident database

comment.narrative:
<p>The project target was achieved. The Database is in operation, and supported strategic decisions on where to strengthen traffic enforcement. The SEINFRA database (ACT Net) is used as the traffic accident database. </p>
<p>It is operating since year 3. </p>

title.narrative: Operationalization of SEINFRA/SITs Pavement Management System

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved already during the second year of implementation. The State has been using the system for improving the network performance during the last years. </p>

title.narrative: Establishment of an appraisal tool to inform decision-making for transport infrastructure investments

comment.narrative: <p>The project fully achieved the target. The appraisal tool became available since 2021 when the maintenance and continuous update of the Logistical Plan and the Tool for the decision-making process was contracted. This indicator is still valid, and the State will continue funding this during the next years. </p>

title.narrative: Change in fatalities and serious injuries on the selected road safety corridors

comment.narrative:
<p>The project highly increased the target.</p>

<p>The revised (corrected) baseline in 2015 was 110 fatalities and serious injuries in both selected corridors. </p>

<p><em>The final data shows 25 injuries and 5 fatalities in 2021 BA-502 and BA-513 roads which showcase a reduction of 72 percent against the targeted 30 percent. </em>Even though improvement works have not been completed, this result is explained by the introduction of enforcement policies and radar installation along these corridors. <em>SEINFRA shared a report on enforcement measures and the importance of the radar installation to achieve this result and increase the attribution of the Project in this result. </em>???????</p>
